reference_fact_schemas.ef4.tick.seed: instrument_id=target entity; session_id=target session; reference_id=x1:B(seed_set_id), caller supplied; effective_start_ns=event time of the last eligible print before the open (utc_ns, strictly before the session open); effective_end_ns=the session open; text=carried sign, exactly one of '+', '-', '0'; price=that print's price coefficient (positive int64, same price_unit and adjustment as the trades batch); factor_num/factor_den=null; known_at_ns=original knowledge, nullable
reference_fact_schemas.note: The seed batch carries a price column, so it needs a price_unit and require_compatible_inputs applies between trades and seed (scale or currency difference INVALID_UNIT, adjustment difference UNSUPPORTED_ADJUSTMENT). Rows within one (instrument, session) group follow the shared REFERENCE order rule. No other fact kind is accepted in the seed role (INVALID_SCHEMA).

mathematics.value_basis: Prices are positive int64 coefficients at ConfigSpec.price_unit.scale (0..18), one currency and one adjustment basis; sizes are positive int64 shares on eligible rows. Every comparison, sum and ranking is exact integer arithmetic; a price is divided by 10^scale only by a consumer, never by the kernel.
mathematics.window: W_set = eligible prints with C - W <= event_ns < C; prefix = prints with event_ns < C - W; both inside [open, C).
mathematics.sign: for eligible prints e_1..e_m in canonical order and reference (p_0, s_0) = (seed price, seed sign) or (none, 0): s_i = 0 if no reference exists; else +1 if p_i > p_{i-1}, -1 if p_i < p_{i-1}, else s_{i-1}; the reference then becomes (p_i, s_i).
mathematics.totals: count = |W_set|; volume = sum q; notional = sum p*q; up = sum q over s=+1; down = sum q over s=-1; neutral = sum q over s=0; net_volume = up - down; net_notional = sum s*p*q.
mathematics.imbalance: net_volume / volume, exact rational then one correctly rounded (half-even) float64; null with zero_denominator when volume = 0; exact +0.0 when net_volume = 0.
mathematics.bounds: volume, up, down, neutral in [0, 2^63-1] (else OVERFLOW only for a selected output that needs the sum); |notional|, |net_notional| < 2^126 < 10^38 whenever volume <= 2^63-1.
mathematics.topk: E = eligible prints; rank by (-p*q, event_ns, order_key, event_id); result = first min(K, |E|); empty covered population gives an empty table.
mathematics.merge: merge(partials) = first K of the sorted concatenation; equals topk(union) for disjoint partitions of a canonical batch.
mathematics.publication: int64 and decimal128 outputs are exact; float64 is the single correctly rounded value of the exact rational.

quality.rule: all applicable reasons retained in lexical order; status follows the first applicable reason in precedence; a value is null exactly when the status is not available; available implies observed == expected

counts.window_outputs: expected = declared coverage count; observed = delivered rows minus rows not ready inside the output's row closure; 0 when a required column is not delivered; 0 and 0 with no batch
counts.sign_based_outputs: as above over every row from the open to C, plus a seed slot (expected +1, observed +1 when the seed is ready) when seed_policy is supplied
counts.top_k: expected = declared coverage count; observed = delivered rows minus rows not ready; 0 when price or size is not delivered while eligible rows exist (this convention is specific to the new producers; the counts of the existing size-ranked output are unchanged)

evidence.window: seed:<reference_id> first when policy supplied and the output is sign-based, then trade:<event_id> of eligible in-window prints in canonical order, cut to evidence_limit; boundary ordinary
evidence.top_k: trade:<event_id> of the retained rows in rank order; boundary closing_auction for a print at event_ns == C with condition closing_auction, else ordinary; at most min(K, n) <= evidence_limit rows, no truncation

mode_rule: known_at and reconstruction availability give identical results with original known_at; batch and full replay only for both producers; merge supported only for the notional top-K under the conditions of DP-K6; update and restore unsupported

acceptance_rules.exact_float64: reference is a dyadic rational with numerator < 2^53: every exact-rational or Decimal120 path produces it without rounding, so the published float64 must equal the hex bit for bit
acceptance_rules.exact_plus_zero: reference exactly 0 from exact integer arithmetic: bit-exact +0.0, never -0.0
acceptance_rules.tolerance: abs(y - r) <= max(8*ulp(r), 1e-12*abs(r)) with r the fixture float64 (the R17 numeric error contract, docs/api/INTRADAY.md, Numeric error contract and capabilities)
acceptance_rules.exact_integer: int64 and decimal128 outputs and top-K rows (price, size, notional) are exact

fixture_notation: compact, NOT canonical wire. open = 0, cutoff C = 100 (W16: 60), knowledge cutoff K = 1000, default known_at 500, price_scale 2, close = C. A trade is {id, ns, ok, p, q} = event_id, event_ns, order_key, price coefficient, size, optional elig=false (eligible=False), ka (known_at_ns; null = unknown; absent = 500), cond (condition), inst/sess = $OTHER_ENTITY/$OTHER_SESSION (a row of another entity or session). Rows are listed in the canonical order (event_ns, order_key) because nothing is sorted. columns lists the delivered payload columns (default price, size, known_at_ns); a column not listed is not delivered. coverage {expected, complete} defaults to the delivered row count and complete. trades null = no batch delivered; [] = a covered batch with zero rows. Window params: window_ns, seed_policy, evidence_limit; seed {price, sign, ka} is the ef4.tick.seed fact (start = -1, end = open by default; refusal recipes may override start_ns, end_ns, inst, sess, fact_kind, count, scale, adjustment); a seed key is present exactly when seed_policy is supplied and null means the role slot is absent. selection lists the outputs requested when it is not every listed output. Expected outputs list status, reasons, expected, observed and, when available, value {exact, float64, hex, acceptance} and witnesses; integers use exact 'n/1' with acceptance exact_integer. The seed witness is written seed:$SEED_REF. Top-K params: top_k, evidence_limit; expected rows are {event_id, price, size, notional} with the notional typed by hand and asserted equal to price * size. Merge fixtures list partitions with their own trades and expected partials, K_param, and expected_merged. Refusals are {base, scenario, mutate[], construction}: a base fixture id plus ordered edits (set, del, append, swap, setitem on dotted paths), so each recipe is executable. Placeholders $ENTITY, $SESSION, $SEED_REF, $OTHER_ENTITY, $OTHER_SESSION are bound by the expander; no fixture carries an instrument, entity, symbol, grid or population identifier. generator: tape of n prints from x = lcg.seed, repeated x = (a*x + c) mod m; per print k: dt = (x>>40)%4 (k = 0: ns = dt, order_key 0; dt = 0: order_key + 1; else ns += dt, order_key 0); price = max(1, price + (x>>20)%5 - 2) from price_base; size = 1 + (x>>8)%1000; eligible = (x>>33)%11 != 0; event_id = g<k>; open 0, C = last event_ns + 1, known_at 0; window fixtures publish the nine totals per window (imbalance as exact rational), top-K fixtures publish the ids for each K and require every index-mod-P partitioning to merge to them. Fixture ids W06, W15 and TK16 (event_id as a last tie key inside one batch is unreachable) were never issued and are not reused, so numbering is not contiguous.

decisions_proposed.decision: Two producers with separate identities, versions and policy labels: `ef4.tape_window_sign` (EQ-158: rolling window totals and tick-rule signed volume) and `ef4.trade_top_k_notional` (EQ-162: notional-ranked largest prints).
decisions_proposed.reason: EQ-162 depends only on EQ-136, is order independent and merges; EQ-158 is an ordered chain with carry and no merge. Different state, readiness and resource profiles must not be coupled.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: one tape producer; fold the window totals into the existing session trade family
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: One evaluation per result, at the config cutoff C. A window length W is a config parameter, so several windows are several configs and several results; rolling means successive cutoffs, each a separate result.
decisions_proposed.reason: The library has one cutoff and one result per config; vector or per-trade series outputs would need a new result shape and a new codec.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: vector output over several window lengths; a value at every trade (series)
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Time window `[C - W, C)`: start inclusive, end exclusive, W an int64 >= 1 with no default. A print at exactly `C - W` is inside, a print at `C - W - 1` is expired, a print at C is outside the session scope. If `C - W < open` every output is `insufficient_history` (no clipping to the open, no spill into the prior session).
decisions_proposed.reason: Same half-open convention as the accepted `[open, C)` scope. Clipping would silently change what W means; spilling would break the reset epoch.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: closed end; clip to open; allow a window spanning the prior session
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: The total order is `(event_ns, order_key)` exactly as supplied (shared validator: equal key is DUPLICATE, decreasing is INVALID_ORDER). No sorting. Prints sharing a nanosecond are processed one at a time in `order_key` order; they are never netted per timestamp.
decisions_proposed.reason: `order_key` is the only certified sequence for equal timestamps; netting or re-sorting would discard it and change the carry.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: net all prints at one timestamp; sort by price; process in arrival order
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Tick rule against the previous eligible print p_prev: sign +1 if p > p_prev, -1 if p < p_prev, and when p == p_prev the sign of the previous print carries unchanged (the zero-uptick / zero-downtick convention). The first print of the chain compares with the seed price when a seed is supplied.
decisions_proposed.reason: Deterministic, quote free, needs only the tape, and a carry removes the ambiguity at unchanged prices.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: unchanged price is always neutral (no carry); quote-based classification
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Reset epoch: the chain starts at the session open. Without a seed the first eligible print has sign 0 and every following unchanged print stays 0 until the first price change. No sign is invented.
decisions_proposed.reason: A sign without a reference is unknowable; a proxy must not pretend otherwise.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: assume up; discard the first print; carry the prior session implicitly
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: `seed_policy` is `none` or `supplied`, no default. Supplied means one `ef4.tick.seed` fact: the last eligible print before the open (price coefficient and carried sign `+`, `-` or `0`). A price change from the seed overrides the seed sign; a `0` seed sign behaves like no seed for the carry. Only tick-class outputs consume the seed. Seed gaps: role absent is `absent_input`, `known_at` null is `unknown_availability`, `known_at > K` is `future_knowledge`, each only on tick-class outputs while count, volume and notional stay available. A seed supplied while the policy is `none` is `INVALID_CONFIG`, never silently ignored.
decisions_proposed.reason: The prior-session boundary needs an explicit fact; ignoring a supplied seed would let two configs differ unnoticed.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: implicit carry from the prior session; seed price only; a default seed
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: An ineligible print is not counted, not signed and never the reference price of the next print. Knowledge still applies to every delivered row, eligible or not, as in the existing session trade admission.
decisions_proposed.reason: Eligibility is normalized by the caller; an excluded print must not move the reference. Knowledge compatibility with the accepted `session.trade.*` admission avoids two behaviours for one tape.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: knowledge only for eligible rows (the EF1 candidate rule)
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Expiry removes a print from the window totals only. The sign chain is a property of the whole epoch tape: prints before `C - W` still set the reference and the carry for the first in-window print.
decisions_proposed.reason: A sign depends on the sequence, not on window membership (W05: the first in-window print inherits its sign from an expired print).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: restart the chain at the window start
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Nine outputs: `tape.window.count|volume|notional` and `tape.tick.up_volume|down_volume|neutral_volume|net_volume|net_notional|imbalance`. `net_volume = up - down`; `net_notional = sum(sign * price * size)` (neutral contributes 0); `imbalance = net_volume / window volume`, so neutral volume dilutes it, and it is `not_applicable/zero_denominator` when the window volume is 0. These are tick-rule proxies: the words buy, sell, aggressor, dealer or inventory never appear in an id, unit or description, the `condition` text is not consumed and no aggressor flag is read.
decisions_proposed.reason: The tick rule infers a price direction, not who initiated the trade; naming it otherwise would misrepresent it.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: name the sums buy/sell volume; denominator up + down only
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: A correction is a new tape revision: the cancelled print is re-delivered as ineligible and the replacement is a new row (new event_id, same or later `(event_ns, order_key)`). The library never patches a result: the corrected tape is recomputed from the seed over the whole epoch, because a changed price flips every later carried sign (W09b). A replacement known after K is `future_knowledge`. Earlier results stay immutable. Batch and replay of the same revision are identical.
decisions_proposed.reason: Accepted foundation: late corrections require a new supplied revision and recalculation; earlier results are immutable.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: incremental patching of signs; in-place revision of a stored result
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Readiness is static per output (not value dependent). count needs the in-window rows; volume adds the size column; notional adds the price column; the six sign-based outputs need every row from the open to C, both columns and the seed when policy is `supplied`; imbalance has the sign-based closure. Counts: `expected` = declared coverage count (+1 seed slot for sign-based outputs when supplied), `observed` = delivered rows minus rows not ready inside the output's closure (+1 when the seed is ready); a missing required column gives observed 0; no batch gives 0 and 0. Coverage with `complete` false or an expected count different from the delivered count is `governed_gap` for every output. A `known_at_ns` column that is not delivered makes every delivered row `unknown_availability` (W10h).
decisions_proposed.reason: Independent readiness with a static, reviewable closure; an unrelated missing operand never blocks a ready output (W08a, W10a, W10b, W10d).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: value-dependent closure (an empty window would ignore the prefix)
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Opening and closing auction inclusion in the session config must be false for this producer, otherwise `INVALID_CONFIG`.
decisions_proposed.reason: Auction prints are not continuous-trading ticks; a tick sign for them has no meaning.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: include auctions as neutral prints
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Count, volume and the three volume splits are checked int64; notional and net notional are exact integer coefficients in currency/10^price_scale published as decimal128; only `imbalance` is a float64, one correctly rounded value of the exact rational. Because every price is below 2^63 and a summed volume above 2^63 - 1 is refused first, a notional sum is below 2^126 (8.507e37) < 10^38: the decimal128 bound cannot overflow once the volume bound holds. `OVERFLOW` is a typed failure raised only by a selected output whose own sum exceeds int64 (RF39, RF40); prefix prints are never summed (W13c); a selection that does not need the sum does not fail (W13d).
decisions_proposed.reason: Accepted rule: exact integer arithmetic, typed failure for unrepresentable sums, no wrap, one final rounding.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: saturate; return null; wide accumulators
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Available outputs list the seed witness `seed:<reference_id>` first (sign-based outputs when the policy is `supplied`), then the in-window eligible prints `trade:<event_id>` in canonical order, cut to `evidence_limit` (0..10000). Prefix prints are consumed but not listed; the cut is visible because `tape.window.count` exceeds the witness count. Unavailable outputs emit none.
decisions_proposed.reason: Bounded evidence with a deterministic order; the prefix can be large and is bound through the input binding and coverage instead.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: list the prefix; fail when over the limit
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Batch and full replay only. Update, restore and merge are `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` for `ef4.tape_window_sign` in v1. The ordered-state parity required by the issue is expressed as a prefix property any later state API must meet (W16 against W05: signs of the prefix prints do not change when the cutoff advances) and as replay parity (W09b).
decisions_proposed.reason: An ordered chain with carry and expiry needs its own state schema and certificates; merging disjoint partitions needs boundary stitching. Both are separate amendments.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: ship an update API now
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: `notional = price_coefficient * size`, an exact Python/int64 product in currency/10^price_scale (the unit string of `session.trade.notional`). It is never a float, is bounded by (2^63-1)^2 = 8.507e37 < 10^38 and so always fits decimal128 (TK09). No bar-derived or adjusted proxy.
decisions_proposed.reason: Ranking in exact integers removes float collapse above 2^53 (TK08).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: float notional; Decimal120; notional from close * volume
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Rank key `(-notional, event_ns, order_key, event_id)`. Equal notional is broken by earlier time, then `order_key`, then `event_id` compared by Unicode code point (not locale), never by size or price. Inside one canonical batch `(event_ns, order_key)` is already unique, so `event_id` only matters between partitions that collide on it (PM04).
decisions_proposed.reason: Row-intrinsic, partition independent and total, so every partitioning merges to the same answer.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: prefer larger size on equal notional; prefer lower price
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: `top_k` is an explicit int 1..10000 with no default; `evidence_limit` is an explicit int `top_k..10000`; the result holds `min(K, n)` rows (the existing bounds and checks).
decisions_proposed.reason: Reuses the accepted bounds so that both rankings are bounded identically.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: a default K; K above 10000
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: New feature id `tape.top_k_notional` in the separate ef4 catalog, value type the existing `TOP_K_TRADES` cell unchanged (rows keep price and size; the notional is derived exactly by the consumer, no new cell field, no new ValueType, Arrow struct unchanged). The size-ranked `session.trade.top_k` is untouched, byte for byte; the two rankings are not equivalent and no equivalence is claimed (TK01 lists both). A consumer distinguishes them by feature id and config digest, not by the cell.
decisions_proposed.reason: A separate name keeps the accepted output and its registry digest immutable.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: add a mode parameter to `session.trade.top_k`; add a notional field to the row
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Identical to the accepted `session.trade.top_k`: eligible prints, the same scope, auction choices (a closing-auction print at C=close is admissible when the session includes it, boundary label `closing_auction`, TK15), coverage, knowledge on every delivered row, positive eligible price and size. A fully covered empty or all-ineligible population is an available empty table (TK04, TK05).
decisions_proposed.reason: The notional ranking must differ from the size ranking only in the key.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: exclude auctions
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Merge takes available partials built with the same policy_version, K, evidence_limit, price unit, adjustment, eligibility policy, entity, market cutoff and knowledge cutoff, concatenates their rows, sorts by the rank key and keeps the first K. The result equals the single pass over the union when the union is a valid canonical batch (PM01, PM02, PM03), is independent of partition order and associative (PM04b, PM06). Counts are summed; an unavailable partial makes the merged result unavailable with the union of reasons (PM05). The same `event_id` retained in two partials is `DUPLICATE`; disjointness of non-retained rows is certified by the caller (summaries cannot prove it). Mismatches use INVALID_CONFIG, INVALID_UNIT, UNSUPPORTED_ADJUSTMENT, INCONSISTENT_IDENTITY or INCOMPATIBLE_VERSION (RF59 to RF69).
decisions_proposed.reason: top-K(union of per-partition top-K) equals the global top-K for a total row-intrinsic key.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: merge unequal K by the smaller K; trust unchecked duplicates
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Batch, conditional merge (above) and full replay. Update and restore are `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` in v1. Corrections need replay because a retained row that is cancelled is replaced by a row that the K-row state never kept (TK13b).
decisions_proposed.reason: A K-row state cannot repair itself after a cancel; update and restore need the certificate machinery of the incremental API and are a separate amendment.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: claim update and restore parity with the size-ranked output now
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: The accepted precedence list is reused unchanged. Reachable here: `absent_input`, `unknown_availability`, `future_knowledge`, `governed_gap`, `insufficient_history`, `zero_denominator`. Unreachable by design: `null_field` (a null eligible price or size is a refusal, an ineligible row is not an operand), `ineligible`, `future_market`, `partial_universe`, `no_eligible_observations`, `empty_universe`. All applicable reasons are kept in lexical order, the status follows the first applicable reason in the precedence, a value is null exactly when the status is not available, and `available` implies `observed == expected`.
decisions_proposed.reason: One status vocabulary across EF2, EF3 and EF4.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: new reasons
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: The EF3 per-output classes: `exact_float64`, `exact_plus_zero`, `tolerance` (R17 contract) and `exact_integer` (all int64 and decimal128 outputs).
decisions_proposed.reason: Same policy, no documented exceptions.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: per-fixture ad hoc tolerances
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Entity, instrument, session, role binding, seed reference and any grid or population id come from the typed `EntityKey`, `ConfigSpec`, input bindings and fact rows, never from a kernel constant. Fixtures carry only the placeholders `$ENTITY`, `$SESSION`, `$SEED_REF`, `$OTHER_ENTITY`, `$OTHER_SESSION`; the harness binds two unrelated sets and requires identical results. Role slot names (`trades`, `seed`) are the contract's closed vocabulary; the seed `reference_id` is the caller's `x1:B(seed_set_id)`.
decisions_proposed.reason: Parameterisation is part of the contract so that adapters, workers and sinks cannot diverge.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: default identities in fixtures or kernels
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Knowledge is enforced identically in `known_at` and reconstruction modes with original `known_at` (`known_at == K` is available; null is unknown; later is future).
decisions_proposed.reason: EF1 and EF3 rule.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: reconstruction ignores knowledge
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Both producers live in `packages/features` (EF4 module, config namespace `ef4.*`) with a separate catalog; `describe_intraday()`, the core session registry and their digests are unchanged; no package version bump.
decisions_proposed.reason: Same precedent as EF3; the accepted session registry digest stays immutable.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: register in the core session registry
decisions_proposed.state: author-decided (EF4-G contract author), pending independent review and owner review

layer_responsibilities.library: admission of the supplied facts, window and closure selection, the tick chain, totals, ranking, merge, quality, evidence and every library refusal; pure and deterministic with exact integer intermediates and one final float rounding; the two producers share only the trade admission
layer_responsibilities.io_ef4: maps ordered TRADE rows with order_key, event_id, eligibility and original known_at, the optional seed fact and the session scope exactly as supplied; maps results (int64, decimal128 coefficient, float64 hex-exact, TOP_K_TRADES cell, status, reasons, counts, witnesses) unchanged; never sorts, deduplicates, nets, imputes, converts scale or currency, derives a seed, chooses a window or computes a sign or a rank
layer_responsibilities.worker_ef4: routes selected outputs with their row closure, keeps per-identity tape order and the sign carry, runs independent partitions and merges only the declared compatible partials, executes one config per complete result, binds inputs and the config digest and persists the library result unchanged; direct, adapter, worker and stored results are identical including refusal class

non_goals: no aggressor, buy/sell or dealer-position claim, field or name; no condition-code interpretation; no quote or NBBO classification
no thresholds, scanners, alerts or ranking policy beyond the stated keys
no default window, seed policy, K or evidence limit
no count windows, no vector or series outputs, no per-trade outputs
no carry across sessions except an explicit seed fact; no end-of-session state output
no update, restore or merge of the window producer; no update or restore of the notional top-K
no windowed top-K, no auction ticks, no aggregation across venues or instruments
no sorting, deduplication, resampling, imputation, price adjustment or currency conversion
no acquisition, file or database access, scheduling or publication inside kernels
no change to `session.trade.*`, to the core registry or to any accepted digest; no new DataKind, ValueType, DTO, codec, validator or error code
no performance, throughput, memory, parity, release or publication claim; the sizing plan names workloads only
no private-source equivalence or source formula
coordinator_freeze: Proposed freeze as ef4-tape1 and ef4-notional1 (v1) for implementation once this PR is reviewed and merged by the coordinator; this document makes no review or acceptance claim. No defaults for window, seed policy, K or evidence limit. Any change to a convention, label semantics, header, role or fixture after merge requires a new policy label and an amendment document.
hosting: packages/features EF4 module, config namespace ef4.*, separate catalog; describe_intraday(), the core session registry and their digests unchanged; no package version bump
seed_kind_rule: ef4.tick.seed is the only new reference fact kind: one fact per target entity and session, exactly when seed_policy is supplied; see reference_fact_schemas
header_ledger_to_be_applied: the 10 headers above, one new reference fact kind and two producers are to be applied by a sibling amendment document after the freeze; units trades, shares, fraction and the currency-coefficient string already exist; value types int64, decimal128, float64 and top_k_trades already exist
amendment_note: Additive producer-set and header-ledger entries needed in the shared contract are recorded here as to-be-applied. No change to shared validators, enums, the core registry or the size-ranked top-K is required or proposed.
